question: Aerenchyma cells are present in _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**common water hyacinth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aerenchyma cells** are specialized cells that have **large air spaces** in them, which allows for **gas exchange **and **buoyancy **in **aquatic plants**.
 
• These cells are present in the **common water hyacinth**, which is a** floating aquatic plant **that can be found in many freshwater ecosystems.
 
• Aerenchyma is especially in the** stem** of the hyacinth.
 
• The stem part becomes** buoyant **and due to this, the water **hyacinth floats **on the surface of the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neem** is a tree species that is native to the Indian subcontinent and is widely used in** traditional medicine and agriculture.**

 
 
• Neem **does not** typically have aerenchyma cells, as it is** not an aquatic plant.**
 
 
 
• **Pea** is a common garden plant that is a member of the **legume family** and is often used as a source of** protein** in human and animal diets.
 
 
• Pea plants do not have aerenchyma cells either, as they are** not adapted** to **living in water.**
 
 
 
• **Cactus** is a group of plants that are adapted to living in** arid environments **and have specialized **water storage structures** and **spines** to protect against herbivores.
 
 
• Cactus plants also do not have aerenchyma cells, as they are adapted to living in** dry environments** and do not need to **exchange gases** in the same way that aquatic plants do.
